parts.latex:
The formula used to calculate the height ($H$) of a structure is given below.

$$H = \dfrac{5p + k}{2}$$

Find the value of $p$ when $H = 11$ and $k = 10$.

solutions.latex:
Substitute $H = 11$ and $k = 10$ into the formula:
$$\begin{aligned} 11 &= \dfrac{5p + 10}{2} \\ 22 &= 5p + 10 &&(\text{multiply by } 2) \\ 12 &= 5p &&(\text{subtract } 10) \\ p &= \dfrac{12}{5} &&(\text{divide by } 5) \\ &= 2.4 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ p = 2.4$$
criteria: Substitutes $H = 11$ and $k = 10$ correctly, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Which of the following formulae could NOT be the result of making $a$ the subject of the following formula?

$$2ab-3c=\dfrac{d}{4}$$

solutions.latex:
Make $a$ the subject of $2ab-3c=\dfrac{d}{4}$.

Add $3c$ to both sides:
$$2ab=\dfrac{d}{4}+3c$$
Divide both sides by $2b$:
$$a=\dfrac{\frac{d}{4}+3c}{2b}=\dfrac{1}{2b}\left(\dfrac{d}{4}+3c\right)$$
These are options C and D. Multiplying the numerator and denominator of C by $4$ gives
$$a=\dfrac{d+12c}{8b}$$
which is option B.

Option A gives $a=\dfrac{d}{2b}+3c$. But dividing the whole right-hand side by $2b$ gives $\dfrac{d}{8b}+\dfrac{3c}{2b}$, so A is not equivalent.

$$\therefore\ \text{option A could not be the result}$$

parts.latex: Which of the following correctly expresses $b$ as the subject of $A=\dfrac{h}{2}(a+b)$?

solutions.latex:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{h(a+b)}{2} \\ h(a+b) &= 2A \\ a+b &= \dfrac{2A}{h} \\ b &= \dfrac{2A}{h}-a \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is option C.

parts.latex: Make $A$ the subject of the formula: $P = \dfrac{A^2 + t}{2}$.

solutions.latex:
Multiply both sides by 2.
$$2P = A^2 + t$$
Subtract $t$ from both sides.
$$A^2 = 2P - t$$
Take the positive square root.
$$A = \sqrt{2P - t}$$
This matches option D.

parts.latex: Express the perimeter of the enclosure in terms of $x$ and $y$. Give your answer in the simplest form.
If Tavi uses 102 m of timber to build the enclosure, show that $y = 18 - x$.

solutions.latex:
The perimeter is the sum of all four sides: $3x$, $4y$, $x$ and $30$.
$$\begin{aligned} P &= 3x+4y+x+30 \\ &= 4x+4y+30 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ P = 4x+4y+30$$

meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:
The perimeter is 102 m, so using part (a):
$$\begin{aligned} 4x+4y+30 &= 102 \\ 4x+4y &= 72 &&(\text{subtract } 30) \\ x+y &= 18 &&(\text{divide by } 4) \\ y &= 18-x &&(\text{subtract } x) \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ y = 18-x$$
criteria: Forms the equation $4x+4y+30=102$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: Make $A$ the subject of the equation $P = \dfrac{A^2 + T}{2}$, given that $A$ is a positive quantity.

solutions.latex:
Make $A$ the subject of $P = \dfrac{A^2 + T}{2}$.

$$\begin{aligned} P &= \dfrac{A^2 + T}{2} \\ 2P &= A^2 + T &&(\text{multiply by } 2) \\ 2P - T &= A^2 &&(\text{subtract } T) \\ A &= \sqrt{2P - T} &&(A>0,\ \text{take the positive root}) \end{aligned}$$

This is option D.

parts.latex: Make $A$ the subject of the equation $P=\dfrac{A^2+T}{2}$, given that $A$ is a positive quantity

$$\begin{aligned} P&=\dfrac{A^2+T}{2} \\ 2P&=A^2+T \\ 2P-T&=A^2 \\ A&=\sqrt{2P-T} \end{aligned}$$
